extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists, zoologists, naturalists and museum researchers studying freshwater Bryozoa (Plumatella and related genera) and collectors identifying specimens
extracted.subtask_description: Morphological and biological criteria used to diagnose, distinguish and record species and genera of freshwater bryozoa (Plumatella, Stolella, etc.), including descriptions of zoarium, zooecia, statoblasts, polypide, types, distribution and biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoarium: overall form and appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: The zoarium in the typical form has a loose appearance due to the fact that the branches are far apart and the ectocyst by no means rigid; zoaria may be adherent, recumbent, cover a considerable area, be dendritic, form gelatinous masses, or be cushion-shaped/sack-like (subfamily distinctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to characterise species and phases: e.g. 'loose appearance' and 'branches far apart' for Plumatella fruticosa; 'entirely recumbent' for P. javanica; 'zoarium often covers a considerable area' for P. diffusa; 'entirely recumbent and often appears to form an almost uniform flat layer' for P. punctata. Notes on whether zoarium is adherent, linear, radiate, or encrusting are diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoarium: method and pattern of branching
rubrics_metrics.description: Branching described as lateral, dichotomous, radiate, crowded (branches pressed together), sparse, or forming linear series without lateral branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branching pattern is diagnostic: 'branching is ordinarily lateral' (P. fruticosa); 'practically dichotomous' (P. emarginata); 'linear series of zooecia without lateral branches' (P. javanica); diagrams (fig. 43) illustrate characteristic branching. Crowding due to environment (e.g. sponge pressure) can alter appearance and must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecia: shape and dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia may be cylindrical, L-shaped, stout, slender, elongate, short and broad, constricted at the base (keg-shaped), or elbowed; diameter and relative length are diagnostic (e.g. diameter more than half a millimetre in P. fruticosa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare typical forms: L-shaped zooecia dominant in P. diffusa; cylindrical with simple dorsal keel in P. fruticosa; 'keg-shaped' in P. allmani. Shape differences often separate closely related species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecia: emargination, furrow and dorsal keel
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecia may be emarginate or not, furrowed on the dorsal surface, bearing a keel (prominent or inconspicuous), or terminally apertured; orifice position may be dorsal even in upright branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence/absence and prominence of furrow/keel used diagnostically: e.g. 'never emarginate or furrowed' (P. fruticosa) vs 'strongly emarginate and furrowed' (P. javanica). Note whether the keel extends to the distal end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ectocyst: thickness, rigidity, pigmentation and texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Ectocyst described as thin/thick, rigid/stiff/soft/flexible, hyaline/glassy/colourless or pigmented (pale pinkish brown, dark brown, almost black), annulated, roughened, tuberculate or polished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ectocyst characters critical: 'ectocyst is thin and never very rigid' (P. fruticosa); 'ectocyst is stiff' (P. emarginata, P. diffusa); 'transparent glassy ectocyst' (P. javanica); 'conspicuous external annulation' (P. tanganyikæ); texture may be obscured by staining. Contractile or swollen ectocyst (P. punctata) is distinctive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal partitions and skeletal details
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal partitions (stout and numerous) of the zoarium are noted as a structural character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'internal partitions are numerous and stout' (P. fruticosa); presence and stoutness of partitions are included in species diagnoses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblasts: presence of free vs fixed
rubrics_metrics.description: Species produce free statoblasts, fixed (stationary) statoblasts, or both; some species rarely produce fixed statoblasts or none at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in diagnosis: 'Both free and stationary statoblasts are formed, but the latter are rare' (P. fruticosa); 'Fixed statoblasts are not found' (P. punctata). Fixed statoblast frequency may vary with colony age/season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblasts: overall shape and proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Free statoblasts may be elongate, broadly oval, truncate, subtruncate, rhomboidal, or variable; capsule size relative to swim-ring and shape of sides/ends are diagnostic (e.g. 'more than twice as long as broad', 'sides convex', 'ends rounded').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare forms: P. fruticosa has very elongate free statoblasts often >2× as long as broad; P. emarginata has elongate and truncate/free statoblasts often 2–3× as long as broad; P. tanganyikæ free statoblasts broadly oval. Shape variability within colonies noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swim-ring and capsule relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of swim-ring relative to capsule: whether the swim-ring encroaches on capsule surface, how broad the free portion is at sides vs ends, presence of solid margin instead of swim-ring in fixed statoblasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'capsule resembles the swim-ring in outline, so that the free portion is not much narrower at the sides than at the ends' (P. fruticosa); 'free portion of swim-ring is not much broader at the ends than at the sides' (P. javanica); 'swim-ring encroaches little on the surface' are diagnostic details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast: surface and marginal features
rubrics_metrics.description: Statoblast margins may be serrated, membranous, possess reticulation traces, have irregular membranous projections, or be tuberculate; dorsal surface may be tuberculate or bear air-cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: fixed statoblasts 'often minutely serrated round the edge' (P. fruticosa); P. tanganyikæ 'ring often possesses irregular membranous projections' and dorsal capsule 'profusely tuberculate.' Such microsculpture is diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast: air-cells and dorsal coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and size of air-cells on the dorsal surface of the statoblast/capsule (cover a considerable part, extend over great part, profusely present, rudimentary air-spaces) are recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'The air-cells cover a considerable part of the dorsal surface' (P. emarginata); 'air-cells are unusually large and extend over a great part' (P. diffusa); some species show rudimentary air-spaces across the dorsal surface (P. javanica).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast: abundance and seasonal occurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of statoblasts produced (profuse, in great profusion, not in very large numbers, variable) and timing (e.g. prevalent in cold weather, 'rains', or at approach of hot weather) are noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to characterize species' life-history: 'Free statoblasts are produced in very great profusion' (P. diffusa); 'not in very large numbers' (P. tanganyikæ); timing of appearance (e.g. P. fruticosa appears after October) helps identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypide: tentacle number and velum structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of tentacles (e.g. 20–30, 30–40, 40–50) and velum features (extent, whether festooned at base, projections on tentacles) are diagnostic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'tentacles number between 40 and 50' (P. fruticosa); '20 to 30 tentacles' (P. tanganyikæ); 'velum...extends upwards for a considerable distance without being festooned' (P. emarginata). Tentacle counts and velum morphology separate species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypide: alimentary canal and stomach shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Stomach described as slender, elongate, comparatively short and abruptly truncated, or rounded at base; alimentary canal robustness noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'stomach is slender and elongate' (P. fruticosa); 'base of stomach is rounded, and the whole of the alimentary canal has a stout appearance' (P. tanganyikæ). Stomach form included in diagnoses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface ornamentation: annulation, tubercles, roughness
rubrics_metrics.description: External annulation (conspicuous slender rings), minute tubercles, minutely roughened surfaces, or smooth/polished ectocyst surfaces are recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. 'conspicuous external annulation' (P. tanganyikæ), 'both velum and tentacular sheath bear numerous minute tubercles' (P. tanganyikæ), 'external surface is minutely roughened' (Stolella indica). These traits help distinguish closely allied taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility/power of zoaria
rubrics_metrics.description: Some zoaria 'possess to a limited extent the power of moving along vertical or horizontal surfaces', with uncertainty about mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted at subfamily level (Lophopinæ). Mobility (or lack) is a behavioural/structural character to consider but may be difficult to observe or interpret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Genus descriptions emphasise features that separate genera: e.g. Stolella 'zoarium consists of groups of zooecia joined together by an adherent rhizome. There is no gelatinous investment.' Lophopinæ zoaria are 'never dendritic but form gelatinous masses'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structure of zoarium (rhizome, gelatinous investment), presence/absence of fixed statoblasts, and zooecial habit (upright vs recumbent) to delimit genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type specimens and repository information
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements whether 'TYPE not in existence', or TYPES held in particular museums (Hamburg, Indian Museum, Philadelphia Academy, British Museum, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence, absence, or location of type material is recorded as part of systematic remarks and affects certainty of identification and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution and locality records
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit lists of regions/localities where species have been found (Europe, N. America, India—with specific localities like Calcutta, Travancore, Punjab, Tenasserim, Igatpuri, L. Tanganyika, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributional data used to assess identity and likely occurrence; statoblasts in plankton or on pond surfaces may extend known range (e.g. plankton gemmules possibly belonging to a species).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology: habitat, substrate, seasonal occurrence, and associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on preferred habitat (still/slow water, stones, stems of water-plants, floating logs, submerged leaves), seasonality ('cold weather', 'rains', 'hot weather'), associations with sponges, rotifers, or other bryozoa, and tendencies like flourishing during specific seasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ecological notes inform identification (e.g. P. fruticosa near surface and edge of water; P. tanganyikæ in shallow water encrusting stones). Environmental factors may modify morphology (e.g. sponge pressure causing coralloides form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraspecific phases, varieties and environmental forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of multiple phases or varieties within species (e.g. three phases A/B/C of P. fruticosa; var. stricta, coralloides; Kraepelin's summer/ autumn phases), and the statement that environment or crowding can produce phase-like changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic remarks note gradations and environmental modification: 'I have seen every gradation between this form and Allman's P. elegans.' Environmental context (embedded in sponge, crowded on plants) can produce distinct-looking phases which must be interpreted cautiously.
